headline: Google Cloud launches Gemini Agent, a universal AI worker
dek: The agent runs across any device and already supports Claude models, SiliconANGLE, The Verge, TechRadar and Tecmundo report.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: One agent for every channel
body: Google Cloud introduced Gemini Agent, an assistant built to work autonomously across any device or channel. It was unveiled at Google's Gemini at Work event (SiliconANGLE, The Verge, TechRadar, Tecmundo).
It is in private preview for a subset of Google Cloud's enterprise customers. Google has not announced a general availability date (The Verge, TechRadar).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Sub-agents and model choice
s3.body: The agent runs in the cloud, so it keeps the same memory and context on every channel (SiliconANGLE, The Verge).

points.t: It spins off smaller agents for specific jobs, each with its own email address and only the context shared with it (SiliconANGLE, The Verge, TechRadar).
Smaller models handle everyday requests, frontier models the long jobs. Anthropic's Claude models are already available (SiliconANGLE, TechRadar).
A recurring task can become a reusable template the agent repeats, from a library customers can expand (SiliconANGLE).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Control for companies
body: Companies can set a hard cap on AI spending in the Google Cloud Billing Console. At the cap, the agent pauses until someone approves going over budget (SiliconANGLE).
Google says every action is logged with real-time monitoring, and role-based permissions help teams spot unusual agent behavior early (Tecmundo).

items.t: Google has not announced when Gemini Agent will reach general availability (The Verge, TechRadar).
Other private and open models are promised alongside Claude and Gemini (SiliconANGLE, TechRadar).
OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse launched last month with similar pitches (TechRadar, Tecmundo).

caption.hook: Google Cloud launched Gemini Agent, a universal AI worker for enterprises that already runs Claude models.
body: Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud's chief executive, said the pitch is to delegate an outcome and come back to finished work, according to SiliconANGLE. TechRadar frames the launch as part of a push toward autonomous "digital employees."

The Verge reports Google already launched a consumer version, Gemini Spark, in May. SiliconANGLE adds that Gemini Agent connects to Jira, Salesforce, BigQuery and Snowflake, and to files on a user's desktop.
